title: Ind-constructible sheaves are closed under extensions
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be $\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$, with the condensed coefficient conventions of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab))$, the module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. All diagrams and colimits are small in the fixed universe of the site and coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ consisting of objects isomorphic to filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$. If
$$0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow0$$
is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] in $\mathcal A$ with $N,B\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$, then $M\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The ambient category $\mathcal A$ has all small colimits and exact filtered colimits. Indeed, [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] supplies the usual closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck coefficient category $\Ab$ and its sheaf tensor product. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] to the small pro-étale site and $\Ab$: the category $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric monoidal, with additive tensor. The ring object $\Lambda_X$ is commutative. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] applies to $(\mathcal C,\Lambda_X)$ and makes $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian. Its small colimits and exact filtered colimits are precisely the axioms in [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian].

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); blueprint Extensions proof, final paragraph, ambient exactness

proof.text: Choose small filtered presentations $N=\varinjlim_{i\in I}D_i$ and $B=\varinjlim_{a\in H}C_a$, with all $D_i,C_a$ constructible, by the definition of $\IndCons$ in the statement. For each $a$ let $M_a=M\times_B C_a$. Pulling back gives $0\to N\to M_a\to C_a\to0$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] in $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the reversed original sequence and $C_a^{\mathrm{op}}\leftarrow B^{\mathrm{op}}$. This is legitimate because the axioms of [def-sp-abelian] are self-dual (kernels exchange with cokernels and monomorphisms with epimorphisms). Reversing the resulting pushout sequence gives the claimed pullback sequence, with the map from $N$ induced by its injection into $M$ and the zero map to $C_a$. For every arrow $a\to a'$ the universal property of the pullback gives $M_a\to M_{a'}$; these maps fix $N$ and commute with $C_a\to C_{a'}$, and uniqueness proves the identity and composition laws.

source.place: Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback construction (1); Tags 08N3 and 08N4; blueprint Pullback to C_alpha

proof.text:
Fix $a$. By the degree-one case of [lem-coef-yoneda-derived-ext-comparison] the pullback extension has a class $e_a\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(C_a,N)$, with Ext interpreted in the ordinary derived category. The final field-coefficient clause of [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity] applies: $X$ is Noetherian, $C_a$ is constructible, the coefficient ring is one of the two allowed field coefficients, and the diagram $D_i[0]$ is uniformly zero in degrees below $0$. It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(C_a,D_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(C_a,N).$$

source.place: Pullback to C_alpha, displayed Ext continuity isomorphism

proof.text: Choose a class $t\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(C_a,D_i)$ whose image is $e_a$ for some $i$. Here the passage from a colimit element to one stage is elementary: the colimit of a diagram of abelian groups is the quotient of their direct sum by the transition relations, as follows by testing homomorphisms out of that quotient; every element is a finite sum of stage elements, and filteredness moves that sum to one common stage. By [lem-coef-yoneda-derived-ext-comparison], $t$ is represented by $0\to D_i\to T\to C_a\to0$. Its pushout $L=N\amalg_{D_i}T$ is short exact over $(N,C_a)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence]. Naturality of the Yoneda-to-derived-Ext isomorphism in its second variable identifies its class with the image of $t$, namely $e_a$. Thus $L$ and $M_a$ are equivalent Yoneda one-extensions. Every morphism in a zigzag of such one-extensions has identity endpoint maps, so [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] makes its middle map an isomorphism. Composing these maps and their inverses gives $L\cong M_a$ as extensions. No such isomorphisms for different $a$ need to be chosen compatibly.

source.place: Tags 06XU (lemma-yoneda-extension), 06XV (lemma-ext-1); homology.tex Tag 010I pushout functoriality; blueprint Pullback to C_alpha, finite-stage extension

proof.text: Use the small undercategory $J=i/I$: its objects are arrows $u:i\to j$, and its morphisms are arrows between the targets commuting with $u$. It is filtered by the three axioms in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: it contains $1_i$; for $u:i\to j$ and $v:i\to k$, choose $r:j\to l$ and $s:k\to l$, then equalize the parallel arrows $ru,sv:i\to l$ by $t:l\to l'$, so $tru=tsv$ gives a common target in $J$; and for parallel arrows $h,h':u\to v$ in $J$, an arrow $q$ in $I$ equalizing their underlying arrows gives a morphism in $J$ equalizing them. It is nonempty, with initial object $1_i$. The diagram $u\mapsto D_j$ has colimit $N$. To check this directly, a cocone on this diagram extends to $I$ by sending $D_k$ through a chosen common target of $k$ and $i$. Two choices give the same map after taking a common target and equalizing the two induced arrows from $k$ and the two from $i$; the cocone relations then give equality. For an arrow $f:k\to k'$, compute the map from $D_k$ using a common target of $i$ and $k'$ and the composite from $k$ through $f$; independence of choices gives exactly the map from $D_{k'}$ composed with $D(f)$. An extension is unique because compatibility with each chosen arrow from $k$ to a common target forces that component. Thus the two cocone universal properties coincide. A constant diagram with identity transitions over $J$ has its displayed object as colimit, since $J$ has initial object $1_i$ and is connected.

proof.text: For $u:i\to j$ set $P_u=D_j\amalg_{D_i}T$, using $D(u)$ and the injection $D_i\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] it fits in $0\to D_j\to P_u\to C_a\to0$. Both endpoints are constructible. The Noetherian consequence of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure], which states part (1) of the unit's cited coefficient-heart lemma in the needed setting, makes $P_u$ constructible. A morphism $u\to v$ in $J$ induces $P_u\to P_v$ by the pushout universal property, using the transition $D_j\to D_{j'}$ and $1_T$; uniqueness proves functoriality. This constructs a small filtered diagram of constructible sheaves.

source.place: Pullback to C_alpha, pushouts of the finite-stage extension and constructible extension closure

proof.text: The maps $P_u\to L=N\amalg_{D_i}T$ induced by $D_j\to N$ and $1_T$ exhibit $L$ as $\varinjlim_{u\in J}P_u$. Indeed a cocone $P_u\to W$ is exactly a compatible family $D_j\to W$ together with maps $T\to W$ agreeing on $D_i$. All the maps from $T$ are the same because $1_i$ is initial in $J$ and all transition maps on $T$ are identities. By step 5 the family from the $D_j$ is uniquely a map $N\to W$; its compatibility with $T\to W$ is precisely agreement on $D_i$. Such a pair is uniquely a map $N\amalg_{D_i}T\to W$. This proves the colimit assertion by its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], rather than invoking an uncited commutation theorem for pushouts and colimits. Steps 4 and 6 therefore express $M_a\cong L$ as a small filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, so $M_a\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Colimit over beta-prime, explicit universal-property verification

proof.text: Take the filtered colimit over $a\in H$ of the exact sequences from step 2. It is exact by the ambient Grothendieck property proved in step 1 and [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The colimit of the constant $N$-diagram is $N$, because $H$ is nonempty and any two objects have a common target, so every cocone on a constant identity diagram is a single map out of $N$. The colimit of $(C_a)$ is $B$ by the chosen presentation. Hence the maps $M_a\to M$ yield a commutative diagram of short exact sequences with top row $0\to N\to\varinjlim_a M_a\to B\to0$, bottom row the given sequence, and endpoint maps identities. By [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma], the canonical map $\varinjlim_a M_a\to M$ is an isomorphism. Each $M_a$ is ind-constructible by step 7, so [det-ind-heart-filtered-colimits] gives $\varinjlim_a M_a\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The definition of this full subcategory is invariant under isomorphism, and therefore $M\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$.
